newsitem.title: KENYA: Rustlers reportedly down Kenyan army helicopter.
newsitem.headline: Rustlers reportedly down Kenyan army helicopter.

text.p: Cattle rustlers shot down an army helicopter hunting them in northern Kenya, killing a government official and two army officers, Nairobi newspapers reported on Saturday.
The government confirmed the crash in the Suguta valley on Thursday and said the three on the helicopter were killed but gave no cause. It said a team went to the area to investigate.
The Daily Nation newspaper quoted police sources as saying a rocket hit the helicopter as it was flying low tracking the rustlers and it exploded when it hit the ground.
Samburu District Commissioner James Nyandoro, 41, and two army officers piloting the helicopter were killed, it added.
Another army helicopter with the Samburu district police chief circled the area and then pulled out to avoid being hit.
The Nation said at least six helicopters were sent to the crash site on Friday and soldiers and policemen from the region were sent in for a joint search for the armed cattle rustlers.
Security forces killed a total of 11 bandits on Tuesday and Wednesday after cattle rustlers shot dead a German tourist having apparently mistaken his vehicle for a police vehicle.
A band of Samburu and Pokot tribal cattle rustlers raided Turkana families in the Merti area of the north on December 3, killing more than 50 people including an assistant chief.
The Nation said hundreds of Turkana cattle rustlers moved to Samburu district in the past two weeks for a revenge attack.
In an editorial, the newspaper said a thorough clean-up of the north was needed to "wipe out" cattle rustlers armed with sophisticated weapons who had perfected their marksmanship.
